name: SEKA Spear RDC frameset
why_interesting: SEKA's lighter Spear: an aero all-round frameset with a threaded BSA shell and a one-piece Rapier bar, listed by two mainland dealers at the same price.

facts.frame: Spear RDC carbon frame and fork with the Wind Eye seat cluster
facts.frame_material: TeXtreme base layers with DIALEAD pitch-based 65T/80T and Pyrofil 30T/40T (FAW69) carbon, plus PMI foam filling
facts.frame_construction: One-mould True-One-Piece frame from about 350 cut plies; internal routing through SEKA's Rapier bar system
facts.frame_weight_basis: Official size-M bare frame without paint or metal parts; fork, bar and seatpost are not included. SEKA lists 729 g ±35 g for a painted size-M Shadow Black frame and says paint adds 20–100 g. Measured: Cyclingnews, size-L frame 758 g; an XHS reviewer, size-M frame in the dark-silver RDC finish 835 g with paint and metal parts, fork 406 g and Rapier bar 338 g; a paint shop, size-S RDC frame stripped and clear-coated 718 g, fork 345 g.
facts.tire_clearance_basis: Official maximum actual tyre width, front and rear, on SEKA's current global and China pages and in the 2024–25 catalog. A 35 mm tyre exceeds that limit; Klein Concept rode nominal 32 mm GP5000s and no wider fit is documented.
facts.stiffness_evidence: SEKA reports a 14.5% stiffness-to-weight improvement and 5% more stiffness than Exceed RDC, plus 109 N/mm vertical compliance, on its own test protocol. Cyclingnews' rig found a size-L bottom bracket less stiff than the tester's steel road bike.
facts.axles: 12 mm thru-axles: front 118.6 mm M12×P1.0, rear 165.2 mm M12×P1.5
facts.cockpit: Rapier one-piece bar in 19 sizes (360–415 mm at the hoods, 80–130 mm stem); the Nanjing dealer lets buyers choose bar and seatpost
facts.seatpost: Spear aero post with 0 or 15 mm offset; clamp fits 7×7 to 7×11 mm rails
facts.sizes: XS, S, M, L and XL, plus racing MR and LR
facts.manufacturer package: Official store package: frame, fork, seatpost, Rapier bar, frameset and bar hardware, and aero bottle cages
